One year in, Verizon (NYSE:VZ) CEO Dan Schulman says the company is "in a fundamentally better position, operationally, financially, and competitively." On the October 26, 2026, earnings call, he noted, "It's been just over a year since I had the privilege to become the CEO of Verizon." Many dividend investors hold this stock, so the claim needs checking against the numbers.

24/7 Wall St.
Customers: Turnaround Earns Top Marks

Postpaid customers pay a monthly bill, and they are the most valuable subscribers in wireless. Verizon reported 406,000 third-quarter postpaid phone net additions, a year-over-year increase of 820%. The company also cited 137,000 net account additions, the best in over a decade. Churn measures the share of customers who leave each month, and Verizon reported consumer postpaid phone churn of 87 basis points. Promotional acquisition costs fell 41%, and retention costs dropped 30%.

Schulman credits Simplicity plans, the loyalty program, and Verizon One bundles, and he questions how rivals count growth: "Net adds are easy if your cost of acquisition goes way up and you give away a free line. I don't consider free lines to even be net adds. I think they're churn waiting to happen."

In the latest periods, AT&T (NYSE:T) added 379,000 postpaid phones with 0.92% churn, and T-Mobile US (NASDAQ:TMUS) postpaid account churn rose 7 basis points to 0.99%. Verizon now leads AT&T on phone additions.

Tutor Perini (TPC) has been one of the most searched-for stocks on Zacks.com lately. So, you might want to look at some of the facts that could shape the stock's performance in the near term.

Shares of this construction company have returned -4.3% over the past month versus the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -0.2% change. The Zacks Building Products - Heavy Construction industry, to which Tutor Perini belongs, has lost 12.3% over this period. Now the key question is: Where could the stock be headed in the near term?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Earnings Estimate Revisions

Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.

Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, Tutor Perini is expected to post earnings of $1.34 per share, indicating a change of +16.5% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate remained unchanged over the last 30 days.

The consensus earnings estimate of $5.39 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +25.6%. This estimate has remained unchanged over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $6.1 indicates a change of +13.2% from what Tutor Perini is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has remained unchanged.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for Tutor Perini.

Comcast (CMCSA) stock has fallen 30% from its highest close of the past year, set in February 2026. Buying now means betting that the overhaul of its connectivity business that management has started will show up in the results. So how cheap has Comcast stock become against its own past?

Comcast Stock Trades Near A Ten-Year Low In Valuation

On September 30, 2026, Comcast's price against its sales was lower than at any other quarter end since December 2016. On that date, the stock also traded at 6.8 times its earnings over the previous twelve months, a multiple it had dropped below at only seven quarter ends during that span.

That discounted valuation accompanies a thinner margin. Over the twelve months ending in September, Comcast posted a 14.7% operating margin, coming in lower than at all but one quarter end in those ten years. Looking at the latest quarter alone, however, the operating margin reached 18.2%, up from 17.7% a year earlier, so profit per dollar of sales held up even as sales fell.

At the same time, the company's broadband business continues to lose customers. Comcast shed 144,000 broadband subscribers in the third quarter, and management said fixed wireless continues to take share while fiber construction remains elevated.

What Is Expected From Comcast's Fourth Quarter?

Analysts expect Comcast to generate about $30.8 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, representing a 4.6% decline from the same quarter a year earlier. This would mark a smaller drop than the 6.1% year-over-year revenue decrease reported in the third quarter, although management called that quarter's revenue flat on a pro forma basis.

Management expects further slight improvement in its underlying financial trends during the fourth quarter. Separately, it expects its theme parks business to return to growth in the second half of 2027.

This improvement must materialize even as Comcast keeps moving its broadband customers to new pricing and offering free wireless lines. The company added 368,000 net wireless lines in the third quarter, and customers taking a free line accounted for about half of its new residential phone lines. Management said it now turns 70% of those free lines into paying relationships.

What Should Comcast Investors Watch In January?

Comcast is expected to report its fourth-quarter results in January 2027. Management also said the separation of NBCUniversal and Sky is on track to finish by the middle of 2027, and that Michael Angelakis will become Comcast CEO next year. Management expects to take a charge of over $1 billion in that quarter, mostly for its transformation efforts.

The deal includes 25 megahertz of mobile-satellite spectrum key to Amazon's satellite-to-phone plans.

FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said the acquisition would bring "even more competition, coverage, and capacity."

AST holds authorization for up to 248 satellites and has partnerships with AT&T, Verizon and FirstNet.

Shares of AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) slipped over 1% in overnight trading late Tuesday as the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) cleared Amazon's $11.5 billion Globalstar acquisition, pushing the tech giant's satellite-to-phone ambitions forward and setting the stage for tougher competition.

ASTS stock jumped 6% on Tuesday to $41.96, but shares are still down 29% for the month.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

Amazon's Satellite Push Clears A Key Hurdle

The FCC's Space Bureau approved the transaction on Tuesday, including the transfer of 25 megahertz of Globalstar's internationally harmonized mobile-satellite spectrum. "This will enhance Amazon's offering of direct-to-device (D2D) services, which will mean even more competition, coverage, and capacity," FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said on X.

The deal will pair Amazon Leo's satellite-building capabilities, launch arrangements and ground infrastructure with Globalstar's existing network and spectrum. The spectrum is key to Amazon's satellite-to-phone ambitions. In its approval order, the FCC said Amazon has applied to operate a global direct-to-device system but would lack the mobile-satellite spectrum needed to run it without the acquisition.

Amazon plans to use Globalstar's assets to expand capacity and bring more services to areas beyond cellular coverage. The FCC said the deal could help close coverage gaps, boost emergency communications and improve data services for businesses and industrial users.

"By approving this deal, the FCC has empowered Amazon Leo to deliver fast, next-gen satellite broadband services, increase competition, and help communities stay connected all across the country," Carr said in the announcement.

Where Amazon's Plans Overlap With ASTS

The FCC's review also highlights how the deal could strengthen a rival to AST SpaceMobile.

In its approval order, the agency cited arguments from Public Knowledge and New America's Open Technology Institute that combining Amazon's resources with Globalstar's assets could create a stronger competitor to SpaceX and T-Mobile's satellite offering, as well as AST's partnership with AT&T. The order also notes AST's ties with Verizon and FirstNet.

Interest rates and bond yields are rising, making dividend stocks less enticing, since investors can earn high returns without having to buy income-producing stocks. But the good news is that this has led to many dividend stocks trading lower lately, pushing their yields higher in the process and potentially setting them up for big gains later on.

Three excellent dividend stocks that are absurdly cheap right now and that are trading below $100 include AT&T (NYSE:T), Pfizer (NYSE:PFE), and Zoetis (NYSE:ZTS). Here's why they can be excellent options for income investors to consider for their portfolios right now.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

AT&T

AT&T's business has been doing well this year, but there simply hasn't been a huge catalyst to make the telecom stock a hot buy. Investors are going elsewhere for high returns, and there are also concerns that Space Exploration Technologies Corp plans to turn Starlink into a major U.S. carrier, potentially disrupting the entire telecom industry.

Those worries have been weighing on AT&T's stock, which is down about 16% this year. Even the company's recent earnings report, as strong as it was, wasn't enough to turn its fortunes around. AT&T posted more than 5% revenue growth in the September quarter, a far higher rate than usual, which should have given investors renewed confidence in the business. But that hasn't been the case, at least for now.

The stock is trading around $21 right now, and its price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 11 is incredibly low. The S&P 500 average is much higher at 23. AT&T's stock also yields 5.3%, providing investors with an extra incentive to buy it today, as it's not only cheap with significant upside potential but also offers high recurring income.

Pfizer

Pfizer's stock has actually been doing well this year, a nice change from previous years when investors remained cautious despite its posting steady, strong results. But even at around $30, this is an undervalued stock.

The healthcare company has been investing in its growth over the years, and while it may take some time for those efforts to translate into stronger top-line growth, the market has been overly punitive, with Pfizer shares down more than 30% over five years.

Its P/E multiple of 39 looks high, but Pfizer has also been incurring nonrecurring expenses as it restructures its operations and aims to get leaner and more efficient. Based on analyst expectations of future earnings, its forward P/E multiple is incredibly low, at just 10. And at 5.8%, it offers an even higher yield than AT&T.
